_note: Values that encode a DECISION rather than a measurement. tools/check_decisions.py recomputes each from its real source and REFUSES if one has moved, because a decision changing is exactly the case where a deliberate act should be required — and editing this file in the same commit is that act. Most numbers in this build move every run; these do not. See own error 48.

kitPin.why: Which build of the shared kit this archive's gates are. It moved inside a commit about gating a chart on 27 September and three builds passed over it unnoticed — own error 48. MOVED DELIBERATELY ON 12 OCTOBER 2026 to e275c14, and the reason is a collision this archive caught in its own scratch build. Moving to a custom domain sets this archive's base to the empty string, and five archives had done it — defranceschi, falco, blazevic, lerena, darcy. SocialHead.astro identified an archive by ring.archives.find(a => a.base === base), so once the SECOND archive moved that key stopped being unique and find() returned the first entry on "", which is the Defranceschi one. This build was emitting ITS name, ITS accent and, worst, A CANONICAL POINTING AT archive.defranceski.com ON EVERY PAGE. A wrong canonical is the one SEO error that hands your pages to somebody else. e275c14 adds kit/lib/ring.js, whose whoami(base) narrows the base match by ORIGIN — import.meta.env.SITE against each entry's url — and falls back to the old first-on-base answer when SITE is unusable, so the archives still on project paths are untouched. THE TELL WAS NOT THE ONE WE WERE TOLD TO LOOK FOR: og:site_name was CORRECT throughout, because SocialHead takes it from Astro.props first (const NAME = site || me?.name) and Base.astro passes this archive's own title, so the prop papered over a wrong `me` on exactly the field the migration recipe said to check. canonical and og:url have no prop behind them and are the honest tells; theme-color is a good third because it comes straight off `me`. Verified here on all four before pushing. The predecessor ffa6ef8 was this archive's own archives.json entry repointed at darcy.defranceski.com and was never deployed.

siteOrigin.why: Where this archive lives, stated in three files that must agree: astro.config.mjs's `site`, site/public/CNAME and site/public/robots.txt's Sitemap line. MOVED 12 OCTOBER 2026 from https://daviddef.github.io/TheDArcy, because defranceski.com is a Pages site served by its own repo and project paths do not inherit it — defranceski.com/TheDArcy/ returns 404 — so a subdomain was the only route. THE CHECK EXISTS BECAUSE THE MOVE LEFT ONE OF THE THREE BEHIND. robots.txt went on naming a sitemap at the old origin while everything else had moved; the build was green and every gate passed, because no gate read it. A reader would never notice and a crawler reads nothing else. CNAME is the dangerous one: this repo deploys by Actions uploading site/dist, and a deploy carrying no CNAME DETACHES the custom domain, so a wrong or missing one takes the whole archive dark rather than leaving a stale line. The gate does not judge whether the address is right — nobody here can — only whether the three agree, and all three failure modes were provoked and seen to refuse before it was trusted.

livingPolicy.why: named-bare: a living person is named and nothing else about them is published. people.js reads living.json's `policy` and falls back to this string, and the key is currently absent, so the fallback is doing the work.

namedLiving.why: The six living people named on purpose, confirmed deliberately by David. Anyone appearing or disappearing here is a change to who this archive publishes.

grafts.why: The two rejected links and how many people hang off each. /how-far-back publishes these counts in a sentence — 71 on a single unevidenced link, 27 on a disproved one — so if the tree moves, that sentence goes stale.

retiredAllow.why: The pages allowed to restate a withdrawn reading, because their subject IS the withdrawal. Widening this list quietly would disarm the retired-reading gate.

livingExemptions.why: Every phrase the living gate is told to let through — the union of living.json's `named`, `namesakes` and `allow`. namedLiving watches who this archive decided to publish; this watches the whole exemption surface, because a phrase added to namesakes is exempted just as effectively and nothing else here would say so.
